title: AI-enabled weather forecast launched
summary: Through the country’s upgraded weather forecasting with artificial intelligence, the Department of Science and Technology is aiming for stronger disaster preparedness.

blocks.text: Launched Tuesday, the PANaHON app of the state weather bureau has integrated AI with the help of US-based Atmo, giving Filipinos access to more detailed, location-specific weather forecasts up to 14 days ahead.
MANILA, Philippines — Through the country’s upgraded weather forecasting with artificial intelligence, the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) is aiming for stronger disaster preparedness.

“This artificial intelligence-based product, which provides detailed weather information, including not just rainfall but also temperature, is extremely important during the El Niño phenomenon, especially for Filipinos who work outdoors,” DOST Secretary Renato Solidum said.
Local government units (LGUs) can provide timely guidance to constituents, especially in the agriculture, aviation and shipping sectors, Solidum stressed.

Atmo chief executive officer and co-founder Alexander Levy said the new forecasting system improves three major aspects of weather prediction: geographical detail, time precision and forecasting duration.

Up to 100 times greater geographical detail is provided by the system, allowing users to distinguish weather conditions across smaller areas, including hills, valleys and mountainous locations, Levy pointed out.
The system offers 12 times greater time precision, generating forecasts at 15-minute intervals instead of the standard three-hour intervals, he noted.

“Compared to standard forecasts that often have a time step of three hours, the new system has a time step of 15 minutes. Every hour that’s four subdivisions. This is a very high level of frequency, especially over the long duration of the forecast,” he said.
Seven weather parameters are displayed in the system: rainfall, accumulated rainfall, wind intensity, atmospheric pressure, temperature, heat index and relative humidity.
Users can select specific locations on the map to view localized forecasts and examine weather conditions through the platform’s available time intervals.
The AI model was trained and fine-tuned using historical weather data from the Philippines to account for the country’s distinct meteorological conditions, Levy said.

Meanwhile, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has partnered with two global climate networks to strengthen the capacity of LGUs in implementing effective climate adaptation and mitigation measures.

The DENR collaborated with the C40 Cities Climate Leadership Group and Global Covenant of Mayors for Climate and Energy to establish the Philippines Leadership on Climate Action and Localization program.

Under the PhilLOCAL program, the three bodies will work together to align local climate policies with national commitments, improve access to climate data and capacity and help LGUs develop investment-ready climate projects that can garner investments.
